subject: gk
question: _________ overloading cannot occur.

options.text: Connecting multiple devices to a single socket
Due to sudden increase in supply voltage
Due to live wire coming in direct contact with neutral wire
By coming in contact with the live wire and the neutral wire through greater resistance.

solution:
The correct answer is __**By coming in contact with the live wire and the neutral wire through greater resistance.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Overloading** in electrical circuits typically occurs due to **excessive current flow** which can be caused by various factors.
 
• Connecting multiple devices to a single socket can lead to **overloading** as it increases the current flow through the circuit.
 
• A sudden increase in supply voltage can cause an **overload** by pushing more current through the electrical system than it can handle.
 
• If the live wire comes in direct contact with the neutral wire, it creates a **short circuit** which can cause an overload situation.
 
• However, coming in contact with the live wire and the neutral wire through greater resistance does not cause an overload because the resistance limits the current flow, preventing an excessive amount of current from flowing through the circuit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• An **overloaded circuit** is a significant safety hazard as it can lead to **overheating** and potentially cause electrical fires.
 
• Proper electrical system design and usage practices are crucial to **prevent overloading** and ensure safety.
 
• Electrical systems should be regularly inspected and maintained to avoid potential overload conditions.
